title: Woman with a Landscape
description:
66 min · Special Pre-Festival Screening
Fostering an outstanding feeling for photography and atmosphere, Matić made an essay about an artist's conflict with the society. It is a story about Šumar, an autodidactic painter with a passion for nudes. Šumar comes to a remote Bosnian village and starts persuading local women to sit for him. Their husbands become enraged, thinking there is more to it than just art.

title: Fatherland
description:
Poland, Germany, Italy, France · 82 min · Open Air
FATHERLAND centres on the relationship between the Nobel Prize-winning writer Thomas Mann and his daughter Erika, an actor, writer, and rally driver. In the summer of 1949, at the height of the Cold War, father and daughter embark on a challenging and emotional road trip in a black Buick that takes them across a Germany in ruins – from US-dominated Frankfurt to Soviet-controlled Weimar. Returning home after sixteen years of exile in the United States, the author has to face not only a divided fatherland, but also deep fracture within his own family.

title: Flies
description:
Mexico · 99 min · Kinoscope
Olga lives a strictly regulated life in a vast block of flats without any friends or relationships. When, out of financial necessity, she is forced to rent out a room, the man who moves in sneaks his nine-year-old son into the flat. To her surprise, Olga begins to form an unlikely bond with the child. Her carefully controlled world begins to shift and, entirely against Olga’s will, these three lives start to become intertwined.

title: Sibel's Advenure
description:
Bosnia and Herzegovina · 62 min · BH Film - Feature Films, Submissions
SIBEL’S ADVENTURE is a feature-length animated film for children that, through a warm, witty, and emotional story, speaks about friendship, togetherness, and responsibility toward nature. When forest animals, faced with serious pollution in their home, seek help from a girl named Sibel and her Eco-Patrol, an exciting adventure begins in which children and animals join forces to try to save the forest and its waters. Through music, humor, and unforgettable characters, the film delivers a powerful message about the importance of protecting the environment and the belief that everyone can contribute to positive change.

title: Motherhood
description:
Romania, Belgium, France · 18 min · Competition Programme – Narrative Short Film, Submissions
From childhood onward, rules are imposed on us, behaviours are dictated to us, and we are told “how to live,” but we are never prepared for the difficulty of “being.” This film explores this question through the lens of motherhood.

title: Atlas of the Universe
description:
Romania, Bulgaria · 85 min · Children's Programme
Ten-year-old Filip travels with his father to the nearest town to buy new shoes for school. When his father gets sidetracked by an old friend, Filip is left to continue the journey alone. A simple mistake at the shoe shop—buying two right-foot shoes—sets him on an unexpected adventure through an unfamiliar world. Too ashamed to return home empty-handed, Filip decides to fix the problem himself. Along the way, he befriends a stray dog, names him after his favorite football player, and finds an unlikely companion.

title: Rose
description:
Austria, Germany · 93 min · In Focus
In the early 17th century, somewhere in Germany, a mysterious soldier arrives in an isolated Protestant village. Slight and modest by nature, his face disfigured by a scar, this stranger declares himself to be the heir of a long-abandoned farmstead and produces a document to support his claim to the suspicious villagers. With the passage of time, he overcomes their doubts and, proving himself to be a hard-working, God-fearing man, becomes a part of their community. However, his quest for acceptance is built on a bold-faced lie.

title: To Hold a Mountain
description:
Serbia, France, Montenegro, Slovenia, Croatia · 105 min · Competition Programme - Documentary Film
In the remote highlands of Montenegro’s Sinjajevina plateau, Gara and her thirteen-year-old daughter Nada return to their ancestral pastures every summer, where they live in symbiosis with the mountain they call “Mother.” Their fragile world comes under threat, however, when the Montenegrin government advances plans for a NATO-backed military training ground to be installed in the heart of this protected landscape. A shepherd mother and daughter proudly defend their mountain from the threat of becoming a training ground for mortar shelling, stirring memories of the violence that shattered their family.

title: Everyone's Sorry Nowadays
description:
Belgium, Netherlands, Germany · 87 min · Children's Programme
On a hot summer day, a  who is girl ignored by her parents meets her favourite actor, Billie King, leading her to self-discovery. A gentle story of finding your place and following your dreams.

title: Maelstrom
description:
Bosnia and Herzegovina · 40 min · BH Film - Special Screening
MAELSTROM is an omnibus of three short films, made as a remake of the eponymous 1964 omnibus by Hajrudin Šiba Krvavac and Gojko Šipovac. Through three wartime stories, it follows characters trying to escape war and its consequences. A father flees with his sons from soldiers, two soldiers search for a way out of a forest far from the front line, and a young soldier tries to save his severely wounded father.

title: Fireworks Wednesday
description:
Iran · 102 min · Tribute To
Rouhi, a young bride-to-be, is hired as a maid for an affluent family in Tehran. Upon her arrival, she is suddenly thrust into an explosive domestic conflict. The wife is convinced her husband is having an affair with a recently divorced woman living next door and enlists Rouhi as a spy, to follow her husband, and confirm her suspicions. What Rouhi discovers, however, threatens not only her employers' marriage but also her own future.

title: Gaja's world – Follow Me
description:
Slovenia · 109 min · Submissions, TeenArena
Sixteen-year-old Gaja navigates life after her parents’ divorce and her mother’s departure on a humanitarian mission. Excited about high school, Gaja faces friendship changes when her best friend Matic moves to England and her first crush, Rok, betrays her at the school dance. Her mother is suddenly kidnapped with some colleagues while aiding children in the war-torn country of Iviris. Gaja, her father, and family friend Inspector Hace enlist imprisoned criminal Alex to rescue the hostages.

title: Pour the Water as I Leave
description:
US, Bosnia and Herzegovina · 75 min · BH Film - Documentary Feature Film, Submissions
A surreal exploration of the war in Bosnia and the unbreakable spirit of seven of her people whose strength to leave was as powerful as the fight to stay. Blending live action with haunting collage animation and choreographed dance, the film follows two lovers whose connection forms as war descends upon their world. Guided by the presence of real-life survivors, their journey unfolds through a dreamlike haze of shifting realities, where memory and trauma intertwine - but so do resilience and hope. The film captures the weight of displacement and the unwavering pursuit of home, no matter where the journey leads.

title: Congo Boy
description:
Central African Republic, France, Congo - Kinshasa, Italy · 95 min · Kinoscope, TeenArena
Bangui, Central African Republic. Seventeen-year-old Robert dreams of a career in music, but civil war is tearing the country apart. When both his parents are thrown into prison, he is left to look after his four younger siblings on his own, juggling daily life, odd jobs, school exams, and concert stages, determined to follow his dream.

title: Don't Ask Me If I Killed
description:
Romania, Netherlands, Germany, Ukraine · 102 min · Competition Programme - Documentary Film, Submissions
When the Russian invasion shatters her world, Ukrainian filmmaker Helena Maksyom lays down her camera only to pick up a rifle — and then takes up both. Across a thousand days at war, she films the moral unravelling of ordinary people forced to kill, and the fragile fight to keep a soul intact when violence becomes a part of daily life.

title: Melt
description:
Austria · 127 min · Ecoscope in collaboration with Green Visions Film Festival Potsdam
Snow and ice, as far as the eye can see: Nikolaus Geyrhalter's new film immerses audiences in a world of white. The filmmaker has visited spectacular locations around the world and met people who are surrounded by these landscapes every day. MELT explores their stories – and the gradual disappearance of the ice that was once assumed to be eternal.

title: The Widower
description:
Bosnia and Herzegovina · 102 min · BH Film - Feature Films, Open Air Premiere
Mirsad is a sixty-two-year-old electrician who was raised and lives in a patriarchal society. His daily routine changes after the sudden death of his wife, Enisa. Mirsad is left alone while his grown children live their own lives. As he tries to get used to a life without his wife, he realises that he took her for granted and had never given her the love and care she deserved. Mirsad’s relationship with his estranged son worsens after he discovers the son lives with a male friend. While his best friend tries to convince him to find a new wife, Mirsad starts questioning his life and his relationships with people, but it is too late for him to change the way he treated Enisa. Soon, Mirsad realises his daughter lives a life similar to that of her mother.

title: Ashes
description:
Mexico, Spain · 102 min · Open Air
Lucila and her younger brother leave Mexico and head to Madrid to reunite with their mother, who left a few years earlier to chase a better future. When the siblings finally arrive, the bitter, suffocating reality that awaits them proves far harsher than Lucila had imagined. Still, she is determined to make the most of this fragile new life.

title: Sheep in the Box
description:
Japan · 126 min · Summer Screen
Grieving Kakeru, their young son, who died in mysterious circumstances, Otone and her husband Kensuke turn to REbirth, a company that assists the bereaved by allowing them to spend more time with their deceased loved ones. Using AI-generated robotics, the company supplies the parents with a state-of-the-art humanoid replication of Kakeru. Initially, the humanoid is barely communicative; it develops rapidly, however, and appears to have memories that are logically impossible for it to have access to. Otone and Kensuke are perplexed to find themselves drawing closer and closer to what appears more and more to be their son.

title: The Dervish And Death
description:
109 min · BH Film - Special Screening, Yugoslav Classic - BH Film
Ahmed Nurudin, a middle-aged dervish and the head of a tekija (khanqah) in the Ottoman Bosnia, receives news of his brother’s arrest for political reasons. In his efforts to help his brother, he must face the authorities and the society, and this challenges his worldview and way of life. As well as psychological, the film explores philosophical questions concerning human life, society and politics.

title: Fjord
description:
Romania, France, Norway, Sweden, Denmark · 146 min · Summer Screen
The Gheorghius, a devout Romanian Norwegian couple, resettle in a village set in a distant fjord, where they become close to their neighbours, the Halbergs. Their children bond despite their different education. When adolescent Elia shows up at school with some bruises on her body, the community asks itself if the traditional education the Gheorghiu children get from their parents could have anything to do with it.Porodica Gheorghiu, rumunsko-norveški par vjernika s djecom, seli se u udaljeni fjord gdje se zbližavaju sa svojim susjedima, porodicom Halberg. Djeca dviju porodica se sprijateljuju uprkos razlikama u obrazovanju. Kada se adolescentica Elia Gheorghiu pojavi u školi s masnicama na tijelu, zajednica počne propitivati da li tradicionalno obrazovanje koje djeca dobijaju od svojih roditelja ima neke veze s tim.

title: Breaking the Waves
description:
Denmark, France, Sweden · 152 min · Gala Screening
Set in the early 1970s amid a small, tightly knit community on the remote north coast of Scotland, BREAKING THE WAVES tells the story of Bess, a young, naive, innocent girl and her profound experience of love. Bess has lived her life protected by her family – her mother, grandfather, and recently widowed sister-in-law, Dodo. Within the confined world of strict Calvinism, she falls in love with Jan, a stalwart oil-rig worker and man of the world. Jan in turn is captivated by Bess's innocence and the purity she radiates. Despite local opposition, the couple marry. For a brief and happy time, the newlyweds live an intense love life but when Jan has to return to the oil rig, Bess is distraught. Long nightly phone calls charged with emotion fail to quell her longing and she prays fervently to God for Jan's return.

title: The Birthday Party
description:
France · 114 min · Summer Screen
Thomas, Nora, and their teenage daughter Ida live on remote marshland. Social contact is limited, as they only have one neighbour, Cristina, an Italian painter. As the two households plan a surprise birthday party for Nora, strange disturbances begin to occur and unease rolls over the marsh.

title: Nightborn
description:
Finland, Lithuania, France, UK · 92 min · Kinoscope Surreal
With dreams of starting a perfect family, Saga and her British husband Jon move to an isolated house deep in the Finnish forest, where Saga spent much of her childhood. As soon as their baby is born, however, despite the reassurances of everyone around her, Saga knows something is terribly wrong. As their marriage starts to crack and Jon struggles to support his wife, only Saga suspects the disturbing truth about their newborn child.

title: Everything That's Wrong With You
description:
Slovenia, Germany, Serbia · 97 min · Competition Programme – Narrative Feature Film
After the emotional collapse that follows her mother’s death, Maruša builds an online bond with Alja, a nurse living in a small coastal town in Germany. Bonding through humor over their shared struggles, Maruša and Alja quickly develop a friendship that is put to the test when they finally meet in person.

title: Blue Heron
description:
Canada, Hungary · 90 min · Kinoscope
In the late 1990s, eight-year-old Sasha and her family relocate to a new home on Vancouver Island, but their fresh start is interrupted by the increasingly dangerous behaviour of the eldest son, Jeremy.

title: Small Things
description:
Croatia, Slovenia, Serbia · 80 min · Competition Programme – Narrative Feature Film, Submissions
During a winter weekend, sisters Anica and Irena, accompanied by Irena’s two children, travel to an island to visit their father and their brother Ivan, a quiet loner. The reason for the gathering is their father’s decision to sell the family land. Confined in the worn-down family house, the members of the family are forced to confront long-suppressed tensions and difficult choices, while one of them will have to make the ultimate sacrifice.

title: Ben’Imana
description:
Rwanda · 101 min · Sarajevo Film Festival Partner Presents
Rwanda, 2012. In the years following the genocide of the Tutsi, community-led trials for justice and reconciliation continue across the country. Vénéranda, a survivor, leads dialogue between victims and the families of perpetrators, helping others rebuild their lives and look towards the future. When she learns of her daughter’s unexpected pregnancy, however, Vénéranda is forced to confront the limits of her own convictions.

After living in Germany for many years, Ahmad returns to his native Iran for a holiday. On the occasion of his arrival, his old college friends organise a three-day excursion to the Caspian Sea. His friend Sepideh invites Elly, her daughter's teacher, who the next day suddenly disappears without a trace. Everyone blames Sepideh for inviting Elly but, little by little, the truth emerges.

title: The Match
description:
Argentina, Spain · 91 min · Dealing with the past
THE MATCH tells the story of the iconic football match between Argentina and England, played at the Azteca Stadium during the 1986 FIFA World Cup. Using rare archival footage, featuring for example Diego Maradona’s controversial hand of God goal, the film reconstructs the event as a living memory as well as the culmination of more than two hundred years of tension, encounters, and conflict between the two nations. From the earliest moments of contact and dispute to the Falklands War as a direct precursor, the film traces a historical journey that reframes what happened on the pitch. In doing so, it subtly contrasts the beauty of football with the lingering absurdity of war, allowing the echoes of both to resonate into the present day.

title: Congo Boy
description:
Central African Republic, France, Congo - Kinshasa, Italy · 95 min · Kinoscope, TeenArena
Bangui, Central African Republic. Seventeen-year-old Robert dreams of a career in music, but civil war is tearing the country apart. When both his parents are thrown into prison, he is left to look after his four younger siblings on his own, juggling daily life, odd jobs, school exams, and concert stages, determined to follow his dream.

description:

title: Everything That's Wrong With You
description:
Slovenia, Germany, Serbia · 97 min · Competition Programme – Narrative Feature Film
After the emotional collapse that follows her mother’s death, Maruša builds an online bond with Alja, a nurse living in a small coastal town in Germany. Bonding through humor over their shared struggles, Maruša and Alja quickly develop a friendship that is put to the test when they finally meet in person.

title: Landscapes of Memory
description:
US, Germany · 78 min · Dealing with the past, Submissions
When director Leah Galant left the United States for Berlin in 2021, she thought she was going on a traditional “third-generation return” to uncover her family’s Holocaust history. After she was detained while filming a pro-Palestine demonstration, however, and subsequently charged with antisemitism, she quickly realised that confronting inherited trauma meant grappling with the present, not just the past.

title: Hen
description:
Germany, Greece, Hungary · 96 min · Adriatic Audience Award
"With great power comes great responsibility" – but what if the hero is just a hen? Escaping from a chicken farm, she finds refuge in the courtyard of a crumbling restaurant. There, she discovers love, confronts the pecking order, and fights to protect her eggs from a greedy owner. Her droll yet touching quest for motherhood mirrors the messy compromises and silent struggles of human lives.

venue: UNIQA Open Air Cinema Stari Grad
description:
Slovenia, Greece, Croatia, Italy, North Macedonia · 100 min · Open Air Premiere
Andrej, a seasoned criminal investigator, faces a shocking revelation when he encounters his estranged brother, Kristian, as a domestic violence perpetrator. As he grapples with guilt and tries to mend their relationship, parallels between Kristian's behaviour and that of their abusive father emerge. This personal turmoil and Andrej's professional life intertwine, leading to substance abuse and strained relationships. A tragic turn of events pushes Andrej to confront his past trauma, which culminates in a heartbreaking confrontation with his father. As he seeks redemption and reconciliation, his life takes another devastating turn when Kristian commits a horrific act, forcing Andrej to confront the depths of familial turmoil and personal responsibility.

title: The Widower
description:
Bosnia and Herzegovina · 102 min · BH Film - Feature Films, Open Air Premiere
Mirsad is a sixty-two-year-old electrician who was raised and lives in a patriarchal society. His daily routine changes after the sudden death of his wife, Enisa. Mirsad is left alone while his grown children live their own lives. As he tries to get used to a life without his wife, he realises that he took her for granted and had never given her the love and care she deserved. Mirsad’s relationship with his estranged son worsens after he discovers the son lives with a male friend. While his best friend tries to convince him to find a new wife, Mirsad starts questioning his life and his relationships with people, but it is too late for him to change the way he treated Enisa. Soon, Mirsad realises his daughter lives a life similar to that of her mother.

title: Gentle Monster
description:
Austria, Germany, France · 114 min · Summer Screen
Lucy, a concert pianist, has just relocated her family from the city to a country house in the hope of easing her husband Philip’s severe burnout. Before they have a chance to set up their new home, an early-morning police visit tears their world apart. Isolated and desperate to protect her young son, Lucy must face the situation alone, trapped between the man she loves and the fear of what he may have done.

title: Foreign Tongue
description:
Canada · 104 min · BH Film - Feature Films, Submissions
After a freak accident leaves her speaking with a Bosnian accent, a North American woman is suddenly seen as a stranger by everyone around her—forcing her to live the immigrant experience she’s never meant to have. FOREIGN TONGUE is a gently absurd and emotionally rich exploration of identity, perception, and belonging.

title: Yugo Goes to America
description:
Serbia, Croatia · 87 min · Out of Competition - Competition Programme - Documentary Film, Submissions
Four millennials, born in the 1990s in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, set off on a road trip across the United States in a Yugo, an old Yugoslav car once labelled “the worst car in the history of the USA.” Traveling through twenty-four states from New York City to Los Angeles, they search for an answer to the question: What does it mean to be the worst? Along the way, they meet people who were involved in importing the Yugo in the 1980s, present-day Yugo enthusiasts, Americans, and immigrants from post-Yugoslav countries. They also come face to face with their own personal history and the ways it is inseparable from the Yugo.

title: Small Things
description:
Croatia, Slovenia, Serbia · 80 min · Competition Programme – Narrative Feature Film, Submissions
During a winter weekend, sisters Anica and Irena, accompanied by Irena’s two children, travel to an island to visit their father and their brother Ivan, a quiet loner. The reason for the gathering is their father’s decision to sell the family land. Confined in the worn-down family house, the members of the family are forced to confront long-suppressed tensions and difficult choices, while one of them will have to make the ultimate sacrifice.

title: Sheep in the Box
description:
Japan · 126 min · Summer Screen
Grieving Kakeru, their young son, who died in mysterious circumstances, Otone and her husband Kensuke turn to REbirth, a company that assists the bereaved by allowing them to spend more time with their deceased loved ones. Using AI-generated robotics, the company supplies the parents with a state-of-the-art humanoid replication of Kakeru. Initially, the humanoid is barely communicative; it develops rapidly, however, and appears to have memories that are logically impossible for it to have access to. Otone and Kensuke are perplexed to find themselves drawing closer and closer to what appears more and more to be their son.

title: Fjord
description:
Romania, France, Norway, Sweden, Denmark · 146 min · Summer Screen
The Gheorghius, a devout Romanian Norwegian couple, resettle in a village set in a distant fjord, where they become close to their neighbours, the Halbergs. Their children bond despite their different education. When adolescent Elia shows up at school with some bruises on her body, the community asks itself if the traditional education the Gheorghiu children get from their parents could have anything to do with it.Porodica Gheorghiu, rumunsko-norveški par vjernika s djecom, seli se u udaljeni fjord gdje se zbližavaju sa svojim susjedima, porodicom Halberg. Djeca dviju porodica se sprijateljuju uprkos razlikama u obrazovanju. Kada se adolescentica Elia Gheorghiu pojavi u školi s masnicama na tijelu, zajednica počne propitivati da li tradicionalno obrazovanje koje djeca dobijaju od svojih roditelja ima neke veze s tim.

title: Nightborn
description:
Finland, Lithuania, France, UK · 92 min · Kinoscope Surreal
With dreams of starting a perfect family, Saga and her British husband Jon move to an isolated house deep in the Finnish forest, where Saga spent much of her childhood. As soon as their baby is born, however, despite the reassurances of everyone around her, Saga knows something is terribly wrong. As their marriage starts to crack and Jon struggles to support his wife, only Saga suspects the disturbing truth about their newborn child.

title: Leviticus
description:
Australia · 88 min · Kinoscope Surreal
Two star-crossed teenage boys must escape a violent entity that takes the form of the person they desire most — each other. An isolated Australian small town hosts the evils of religious fanaticism and its consequences for queer youth, creating an atmosphere that is chilling and near-claustrophobic.

North Macedonia, Serbia, Slovenia · 105 min · Competition Programme – Narrative Feature Film
Seventeen-year-old Sara is hiding a secret during a school trip. When the trip spirals out of control and she witnesses her friend Lina being sexually assaulted, the two girls try to break the cycle of casual violence. This seals an everlasting bond between them.

title: MASTERCLASS: Rodrigo Sorogoyen
description:
90 min
Moderated Interview in the form of a conversation with the director of the film "The Beloved" Rodrigo Sorogoyen, where he will share his knowledge and experiences with both the Festival audience and participants.

title: La Gradiva
description:
France, Italy · 145 min · Kinoscope
Some French high-school students travel to Naples on a school trip to discover the ruins of Pompeii and the bodies petrified by the eruption of Mount Vesuvius. There, they are drawn into a dizzying descent. One by one, they are swept up in desire and anger, until they surrender completely.

title: Everytime
description:
Austria, Germany · 121 min · Competition Programme – Narrative Feature Film
A tragedy brings a mother, a daughter, and a teenage boy together. Struggling with blame and forgiveness, the unlikely trio takes a trip to Tenerife for a family holiday that never happens. Under the glow of the sun, past and present quietly start to overlap.

description:
Belgium, Lebanon, Palestine, Qatar, Saudi Arabia · 100 min · Sarajevo Film Festival Partner Presents
In the quiet fog of the Beqaa Valley, on the border between Lebanon and Syria, someone sets fire to a truck. In this tightly woven Bedouin community, Gamra is gone, maybe hiding – maybe running. As her cousin Yasser sets out to find her, he runs over a man from a rival tribe. His sisters Rim and Jawaher are chosen to walk into the night as an offering. Will their sacrifice be enough to preserve the fragile balance, or will this burning flame spread through the entire village?

description:
Netherlands · 88 min · Children's Programme, Submissions
When Meissy's (11) father reappears in their town after years of absence, she's immediately thrilled. Going against her mother Lucy's wishes, she secretly visits him and is enchanted by his colorful, wandering life on the streets, full of fantasy, origami cranes, and special encounters. But then she discovers what her mother had been warning her about: her father is a schizophrenic and he suffers from hallucinations and grandiose delusions.

title: The Pledge from the Bronze Age
description:
Bosnia and Herzegovina · 89 min · BH Film - Documentary Feature Film, Submissions
Confronting the ruins of a house burned down in the war turns into an archaeological excavation of one's own soul, where the unexpected discovery of Bronze Age bones and the wiping away of war's ashes merge into a singular oath and truth about all of us.

title: CASE STUDY: The Wedding
description:
90 min
Regional co-productions can take years to move from idea to greenlight. The Wedding went through seven years of financing and development before becoming the most-watched film in Croatian cinema history, with more than 2.4 million admissions in cinemas to date, as well as a major box-office success across the region. This case study examines what sustains a producer and director through such an extended development period, and what it takes for a small, deeply local story to find an audience on such a remarkable scale.
Bringing together director Igor Šeregi, producer Ivan Kelava, and actors Dragan Bjelogrlić and Rene Bitorajac, the conversation traces the film’s trajectory from its original idea in 2016 through years of development and financing to record-breaking box-office success and international distribution, a journey ten years in the making.

title: The Loneliest Man in Town
description:
Austria · 86 min · In Focus
Blues musician Al Cook lives surrounded by memories: in his apartment and basement studio, books, videotapes, and vinyl records fill the space, all that remains of a life once fully lived, a place where time seems to stand still. Outside, the world carries on without him. But when a ruthless real estate company targets his home for demolition, his refuge collapses and he is forced to face the ruins of his existence. As he lets go of the treasures of his life one by one, Al Cook confronts a painful question: how do you move forward when your memories are all you have left? In the face of total loss, he chooses a radical new beginning.

title: Electing Ms Santa
description:
Moldova, Romania · 95 min · Competition Programme - Documentary Film, Submissions
Politics in Moldova is no longer just a man's game – at least, not in Elena’s village. By launching a bold bid for local office, the forty-two-year-old woman becomes the uncomfortable face of change. Her decision to run is more than just a political campaign: it is the story of a woman daring to dismantle patriarchal boundaries while her entire nation stands on the threshold of historic transformation, edging closer to the European Union.

In the late 1990s, eight-year-old Sasha and her family relocate to a new home on Vancouver Island, but their fresh start is interrupted by the increasingly dangerous behaviour of the eldest son, Jeremy.

title: The Past
description:
France, Italy · 130 min · Tribute To
Following a four-year separation, Ahmad returns to Paris from Tehran, upon his French wife Marie’s request, in order to finalise their divorce proceedings. During his brief stay, Ahmad discovers the conflictual nature of Marie’s relationship with her daughter Lucie. Ahmad’s efforts to improve this relationship soon unveil a secret from their past.

description:
Indonesia, France · 63 min · House of Shorts Special Screening
Continuing the concept initiated in 2013 by La Factory at the Directors' Fortnight of the Festival de Cannes , the Next Step Studio programme supports emerging new voices in cinema around the world. Each year, it takes place in a different country and highlights local filmmaking, bringing together eight emerging directors – four local and four international – to co-write and co-direct four short films. This year, Next Step Studio highlights Indonesia. These four short films were presented in La Semaine de la Critique at Cannes in 2026. HOLY CROWD follows Ratna, who rises from the dead during her own funeral, triggering a frenzy of miracles, faith, and exploitation. ORIGINAL WOUND tells the story of a brother and sister who confront memories of abuse and care after the death of their mother. ANNISA is about a blind teenage girl who finds an unexpected way to make her voice heard amid a neighbourhood celebration. Finally, MOTHERS ARE MOTHERING follows a woman trapped in an abusive marriage as memory, desire, and myth intertwine in her search for freedom.

title: Gaja's world – Follow Me
description:
Slovenia · 109 min · Submissions, TeenArena
Sixteen-year-old Gaja navigates life after her parents’ divorce and her mother’s departure on a humanitarian mission. Excited about high school, Gaja faces friendship changes when her best friend Matic moves to England and her first crush, Rok, betrays her at the school dance. Her mother is suddenly kidnapped with some colleagues while aiding children in the war-torn country of Iviris. Gaja, her father, and family friend Inspector Hace enlist imprisoned criminal Alex to rescue the hostages.

title: Somebody Missing
description:
Bosnia and Herzegovina · 63 min · BH Film - Documentary Feature Film, Submissions
Thirty years after four young girls disappeared, memory becomes the only bridge between what was and what could have been.

title: Objet a
description:
Germany, Luxembourg, Greece · 99 min · Kinoscope
Ingeborg and Adam are visionary hand surgeons bound by love, control, and irresistible fixations. She is compelled to steal objects; he longs to become one. When an accident brings the enigmatic Gaia into their lives, unexpected desires begin to take shape, unsettling the careful balance that has long defined their relationship.

title: Not a Hero
description:
India, Singapore · 98 min · Children's Programme
Mivan, 11, a city raised boy, is sent to his ancestral village to stay withhis young aunt, Pahi. Used to the speed and comforts of urban life, he finds the village slow, unfamiliar, and difficult to accept. His relationship with Pahi is distant, shaped by unspoken tensions and unresolved feelings from the past. As Mivan is drawn into village routines, school, and new friendships, he begins to experience a world where time moves differently and nothing comes easily.

title: When I Get Out
description:
Slovenia · 106 min · Competition Programme - Documentary Film, Submissions
The film's director and a psychiatrist go to Dob Prison in central Slovenia. The director believes there are stories locked up there, while the psychiatrist believes his psychodrama method can open up a redemptive creative space and a glimpse into the convicts' future. A liberated territory in a closed area?

title: Identity
description:
Croatia · 74 min · Dealing with the past, Submissions
Ajna, Alen, and Lejla were born after their mothers were raped in the war. Ajna was kept by her mother, while Alen and Lejla were adopted. They grew up and lived differently and learned the truth about their origins in various ways, but they are bound by an inner feeling that is incomprehensible to all other people. Their stories intertwine through the fight for the legal status of war victims, very personal searches and public appearances, while the film explores identity and trauma, as well as the possibilities of community and belonging, through archives and an observational approach.

title: Made in EU
description:
Bulgaria, Germany, Czechia · 102 min · Adriatic Audience Award
Iva, who works in a clothing factory in rural Bulgaria, is battling a persistent, mysterious illness. When it is revealed that she has contracted the first case of COVID in her small town, the news spirals into an endless j’accuse – first from the factory owners eager to shift responsibility, then from her fellow co-workers, her son, and eventually the entire community, despite the fact that Iva hasn’t left her small town in years. With her public demonisation escalating as the first victims of the virus emerge, Iva is quickly turned into a social outcast.

title: No Good Men
description:
Germany, France, Norway, Denmark, Afghanistan · 103 min · Open Air
Afghanistan, immediately before the return of the Taliban in 2021. Naru, the only camerawoman at Kabul’s main TV station, struggles to keep custody of her three-year-old son after leaving her husband, a serial cheater. Convinced no good men exist in her country, Naru is caught off guard when Qodrat, Kabul TV’s most respected journalist, gives her a career opportunity. As the two criss-cross the city reporting on its last days of freedom, sparks fly and Naru starts to doubt herself: Might there actually be a good man out there?

venue: UNIQA Open Air Cinema Stari Grad
description:
Croatia, Serbia · 97 min · Open Air Premiere
Tonina, a caring and self-confident accountant, runs her company together with her husband and daughter and pulls all the strings for the family logistics. Along with all her obligations, Tonina is taking care of her demented and bedridden mother. Her younger sister Tajana and her family have a much more easygoing and less ambitious approach to life. The two sisters clash when Tonina secretly buys out a part of their island family house from their cousin Željka, even though the sisters had agreed to buy it together. One year later, Tonina and Tajana try to reconcile for their mother’s birthday, but tensions resurface.

title: Lachtara-Longing
description:
Poland, Greece · 127 min · Special Screenings, Submissions
2015: Europe in the financial and migration crisis. Piotr, a Polish stockbroker, finds after 28 years his father, Jorgos—an eccentric Greek musician. Together, they set off in an old car from Greece to Poland to settle a family inheritance. Everything divides them: money, temperament, memory, and unspoken regret. During the journey, the demons of: the Greek Civil War, emigration and their separation come back. When they pick up a Syrian refugee girl, the journey takes on an unexpected dynamic. The father and son must face a family secret whose roots lie in the events in Poland from 1987...

title: The Match
description:
Argentina, Spain · 91 min · Dealing with the past
THE MATCH tells the story of the iconic football match between Argentina and England, played at the Azteca Stadium during the 1986 FIFA World Cup. Using rare archival footage, featuring for example Diego Maradona’s controversial hand of God goal, the film reconstructs the event as a living memory as well as the culmination of more than two hundred years of tension, encounters, and conflict between the two nations. From the earliest moments of contact and dispute to the Falklands War as a direct precursor, the film traces a historical journey that reframes what happened on the pitch. In doing so, it subtly contrasts the beauty of football with the lingering absurdity of war, allowing the echoes of both to resonate into the present day.

title: Fjord
venue: BH Telecom Open Air Cinema Centar
description:
Romania, France, Norway, Sweden, Denmark · 146 min · Summer Screen
The Gheorghius, a devout Romanian Norwegian couple, resettle in a village set in a distant fjord, where they become close to their neighbours, the Halbergs. Their children bond despite their different education. When adolescent Elia shows up at school with some bruises on her body, the community asks itself if the traditional education the Gheorghiu children get from their parents could have anything to do with it.Porodica Gheorghiu, rumunsko-norveški par vjernika s djecom, seli se u udaljeni fjord gdje se zbližavaju sa svojim susjedima, porodicom Halberg. Djeca dviju porodica se sprijateljuju uprkos razlikama u obrazovanju. Kada se adolescentica Elia Gheorghiu pojavi u školi s masnicama na tijelu, zajednica počne propitivati da li tradicionalno obrazovanje koje djeca dobijaju od svojih roditelja ima neke veze s tim.

title: Sheep in the Box
description:
Japan · 126 min · Summer Screen
Grieving Kakeru, their young son, who died in mysterious circumstances, Otone and her husband Kensuke turn to REbirth, a company that assists the bereaved by allowing them to spend more time with their deceased loved ones. Using AI-generated robotics, the company supplies the parents with a state-of-the-art humanoid replication of Kakeru. Initially, the humanoid is barely communicative; it develops rapidly, however, and appears to have memories that are logically impossible for it to have access to. Otone and Kensuke are perplexed to find themselves drawing closer and closer to what appears more and more to be their son.

title: The Will
description:
Bosnia and Herzegovina · 109 min · BH Film - Feature Films
THE WILL is a humorous and heartfelt story set in a Bosnian village and the industrial city of Zenica in the early 1990s. In its own distinctive way, it explores the importance of having a will and the consequences of not having one within the local cultural context. Through the lives of ordinary people, the film presents a series of small conflicts and misunderstandings over inheritance, tradition, and human relationships, where long-held customs collide with a reality shaped by human weaknesses-gambling, gossip, love, and petty theft.The protagonist, Asad, is left without his father's inheritance and must find his way in the world of industrial Zenica, local taverns, and the everyday challenges of village life. Along the way, he is helped by his best friend, Dževad, a charming character who is dealing with his own struggles and is always looking for the quickest shortcut to a solution.

title: No Good Men
description:
Germany, France, Norway, Denmark, Afghanistan · 103 min · Open Air
Afghanistan, immediately before the return of the Taliban in 2021. Naru, the only camerawoman at Kabul’s main TV station, struggles to keep custody of her three-year-old son after leaving her husband, a serial cheater. Convinced no good men exist in her country, Naru is caught off guard when Qodrat, Kabul TV’s most respected journalist, gives her a career opportunity. As the two criss-cross the city reporting on its last days of freedom, sparks fly and Naru starts to doubt herself: Might there actually be a good man out there?

title: Everytime
description:
Austria, Germany · 121 min · Competition Programme – Narrative Feature Film
A tragedy brings a mother, a daughter, and a teenage boy together. Struggling with blame and forgiveness, the unlikely trio takes a trip to Tenerife for a family holiday that never happens. Under the glow of the sun, past and present quietly start to overlap.

title: The Balkan Cowboy
description:
Ireland, Croatia · 93 min · Competition Programme - Documentary Film, Submissions
Artist Dragana Jurišić travels to the town of Bijeljina, Bosnia and Herzegovina, to stage a short film in the style of the mythical cult Western director Hari Džekson (Harry Jackson). In an attempt to uncover the story of Džekson’s life and legacy, Jurišić embarks on making a Western with the local community. She meets his former collaborators, family members, and local residents, piecing together memories of Džekson’s town before the war and getting to know its inhabitants today.  The resulting documentary becomes an exploration of the impact of war on Džekson, Jurišić herself, and the town. It also asks whether the spirit of Hari Džekson still exists today.

title: Leviticus
description:
Australia · 88 min · Kinoscope Surreal
Two star-crossed teenage boys must escape a violent entity that takes the form of the person they desire most — each other. An isolated Australian small town hosts the evils of religious fanaticism and its consequences for queer youth, creating an atmosphere that is chilling and near-claustrophobic.

title: Never After Dark
description:
Japan · 104 min · Kinoscope Surreal
A wandering medium, Airi spends her life guiding restless spirits out of the world of the living. Summoned to an isolated country house, she comes face to face with a grotesque apparition with powers that defy her experience. As Airi digs deeper into the house’s past, a secret comes to light — and Airi finds herself hunted by a far more unpredictable force. For the first time, her greatest adversary is not the supernatural, but the living.

title: From Nothing to Nowhere
description:
Croatia · 72 min · Midnight Screenings
Dante, an operator of a semi-submersible for tourists, finds a camera that was left in his apartment by a Czech tourist and decides to use it to film a documentary about the construction of a high-speed highway connecting Split and Omiš and the Omiš beltway. His research quickly introduces him to a gallery of eccentric characters: guru Vico, English artist Frifsteen, and his mechanical chicken. Vico has a theory that traffic jams are artificially created to justify boring a tunnel through the mountain to find a Tesla oscillator.

title: Dua
description:
Kosovo, Switzerland, France · 101 min · Competition Programme – Narrative Feature Film
Prishtina, Kosova, late 1990s. As war looms and ethnic tensions escalate, 13-year-old Dua struggles to find her place among her peers and within her changing body. After an incident shakes her community, she becomes a target herself and bonds with a fearless girl, Maki, who draws her toward an unexpected form of resistance. Between the daily violence and the growing threat of exile, there is little room for quiet awakenings.

title: Electing Ms Santa
description:
Moldova, Romania · 95 min · Competition Programme - Documentary Film, Submissions
Politics in Moldova is no longer just a man's game – at least, not in Elena’s village. By launching a bold bid for local office, the forty-two-year-old woman becomes the uncomfortable face of change. Her decision to run is more than just a political campaign: it is the story of a woman daring to dismantle patriarchal boundaries while her entire nation stands on the threshold of historic transformation, edging closer to the European Union.

title: The Dreamed Adventure
description:
Germany, France, Bulgaria, Austria · 167 min · Kinoscope
In Svilengrad, a small town on the Bulgarian border, Veska crosses paths with Said, an old acquaintance whose car has been stolen. Offering her help, Veska brings him along to the excavation site where she is working as an archaeologist. As they reconnect, she is pulled more into the shady world Said has emerged from, and she soon embarks on an exploration of the criminal ties lurking beneath the surface of this seemingly innocent town on the outskirts of Europe. As figures from her past start to close in, Veska is forced to confront the truth about the town and her experiences.

title: When I Get Out
description:
Slovenia · 106 min · Competition Programme - Documentary Film, Submissions
The film's director and a psychiatrist go to Dob Prison in central Slovenia. The director believes there are stories locked up there, while the psychiatrist believes his psychodrama method can open up a redemptive creative space and a glimpse into the convicts' future. A liberated territory in a closed area?

title: Souraya Mon Amour
description:
Lebanon, Qatar · 81 min · Sarajevo Film Festival Partner Presents
SOURAYA MON AMOUR invites us into the private world of Souraya Baghdadi – a world filled with dance, film, meditation, memories, and deep reflection. Her story with her husband, Maroun, began in 1981 during the filming of LITTLE WARS in war-torn Beirut, when Souraya played the lead role. After the film had its premiere at Cannes, they moved to Paris and started a life together. But in December 1993, Maroun died suddenly and mysteriously, just as Souraya was expecting their third child. Three decades later, Souraya revisits the fragments of a life suspended. Through distant conversations, tender archives, and moments of introspection, a love story unfolds, unveiling the fragile tension of a bond shaped by presence – and even more profoundly, by absence.

North Macedonia, Serbia, Slovenia · 105 min · Competition Programme – Narrative Feature Film
Seventeen-year-old Sara is hiding a secret during a school trip. When the trip spirals out of control and she witnesses her friend Lina being sexually assaulted, the two girls try to break the cycle of casual violence. This seals an everlasting bond between them.

title: Love Dog
description:
Poland, Mexico, US · 84 min · The Béla Tarr in Sarajevo Tribute
After finishing a job on a Texas oil rig, John returns to his hometown in Mississippi, where he will confront not only his own repressed trauma, but that of a society grieving dying American myths.

title: Not a Hero
description:
India, Singapore · 98 min · Children's Programme
Mivan, 11, a city raised boy, is sent to his ancestral village to stay withhis young aunt, Pahi. Used to the speed and comforts of urban life, he finds the village slow, unfamiliar, and difficult to accept. His relationship with Pahi is distant, shaped by unspoken tensions and unresolved feelings from the past. As Mivan is drawn into village routines, school, and new friendships, he begins to experience a world where time moves differently and nothing comes easily.

title: MASTERCLASS: Woody Harrelson
description: Moderated Interview in the form of a conversation with Honorary Heart of Sarajevo Award Recipient Woody Harrelson, where he will share his knowledge and experiences with both the Festival audience and participants.

title: Promised Spaces
description:
France, Germany, Serbia, Cambodia · 78 min · In Focus
Sleepless from the heat, Sokun leaves his crowded construction dormitory and joins a community of fellow workers living in one of many unfinished high-rises. One such tower becomes the long-awaited luxury home for its first tenant, Seda, who soon feels isolated in the vast gated complex.

title: Mouse
description:
US · 120 min · TeenArena
It’s 2002, and senior year of high school is on the horizon for best friends Minnie and Callie. Their relationship is suddenly upended at the start of the summer. Left rudderless without her charismatic best friend, Minnie starts to form a complicated friendship with Callie’s mother.

title: La Gradiva
description:
France, Italy · 145 min · Kinoscope
Some French high-school students travel to Naples on a school trip to discover the ruins of Pompeii and the bodies petrified by the eruption of Mount Vesuvius. There, they are drawn into a dizzying descent. One by one, they are swept up in desire and anger, until they surrender completely.

title: The Salesman
description:
Iran, France · 125 min · Tribute To
Forced out of their apartment due to dangerous works on a neighbouring building, Emad and Rana move into a new flat in the centre of Tehran. An incident linked to the previous tenant dramatically changes the young couple’s life.

title: Survival
description:
Bosnia and Herzegovina · 83 min · BH Film - Documentary Feature Film, Submissions
SURVIVAL is an emotional documentary exploring the power of music during the siege of Bihać during the war of the 1990s. At the center of the story is Sejfo, frontman of the band Okus Meda, who together with a group of musicians and singers creates the song "Ljubav je svijet" ("Love Is the World") as a symbol of hope, resistance, and life in a time of fear and destruction. Through personal testimonies, archival footage, and the story of how the song came to be under siege, the film shows how music became a way of surviving, preserving identity, and preserving humanity. SURVIVAL is a powerful story of courage, togetherness, and art that was louder than war.

title: Manhunt
description:
Canada · 103 min · Kinoscope
Two young men flee their dead-end lives on a road trip into the northern frontier. Recasting true crime as parable, MANHUNt explores loneliness, masculinity, and the colonial urge to begin anew – until the search for meaning erupts into violence.

title: Peacemaker
description:
Croatia · 100 min · Dealing with the past
In 1991, on the outskirts of Tenja in Croatia, Josip Reihl Kir – the chief of the Osijek Police Department, a man dedicated to negotiations and avoiding war – was assassinated. Told through the statements of witnesses and archival materials from the era, PEACEMAKER is a film about the last few months of his life, at the dawn of the bloody Croatian War of Independence, which Kir had been trying hard to prevent. Today, more than thirty years later, many elements of this assassination remain unclear, and the possible perpetrators are still unknown.

title: Objet a
description:
Germany, Luxembourg, Greece · 99 min · Kinoscope
Ingeborg and Adam are visionary hand surgeons bound by love, control, and irresistible fixations. She is compelled to steal objects; he longs to become one. When an accident brings the enigmatic Gaia into their lives, unexpected desires begin to take shape, unsettling the careful balance that has long defined their relationship.

title: Only Beautiful Things to Look At
description:
Slovakia, Czechia, Hungary · 88 min · Adriatic Audience Award
Ingrid, an elegant doctor, works in a remote district hospital in the mid-1980s. Trapped in an exhausting marriage and a stagnant career, she devotes most of her time to her patients. She delivers babies and performs abortions. She also carries out sterilisations on Romani women — without them fully understanding the consequences. A new friendship with Agáta, a young and free-spirited orderly, compels Ingrid to see things in a different light. Will she begin to question the rules she has so far followed with indifference?

title: Congo Boy
description:
Central African Republic, France, Congo - Kinshasa, Italy · 95 min · Kinoscope, TeenArena
Bangui, Central African Republic. Seventeen-year-old Robert dreams of a career in music, but civil war is tearing the country apart. When both his parents are thrown into prison, he is left to look after his four younger siblings on his own, juggling daily life, odd jobs, school exams, and concert stages, determined to follow his dream.

title: Welcome to Sarajevo
description:
UK, US · 100 min · Open Air
During the war in Bosnia, British foreign correspondent Michael Henderson is stationed in the besieged city of Sarajevo. After discovering an orphanage on the front line, where children live under constant artillery fire, he reports repeatedly on their plight, urging the international community to act. Frustrated by the world's inaction and unable to remain a detached observer, Henderson decides to smuggle one of the children to safety in England.

title: Hidden People
venue: UNIQA Open Air Cinema Stari Grad
description:
Slovenia, Serbia, Iceland · 97 min · Open Air Premiere
Guti (35) and Sig (50) wake up beaten, hungover, and handcuffed together on a riverbank near Ljubljana. Sig, obviously a tourist, suffers from memory loss and can’t remember where he is from and why he is - as he thinks - stuck in Slovakia. Together with Guti, they embark on a journey to recover Sig’s passport and identity and, in the meantime, work on Guti’s dream project: a river raft that will hopefully rebuild Guti’s life that has fallen victim to bad divorce, failed bank loans, vicious bureaucracy, and many, many bad neighbors.

title: Another Day
description:
France · 120 min · Summer Screen
Garance is a gifted young actor whose raw magnetism and vibrant spirit have yet to earn her the recognition she craves. Living paycheque to paycheque in a small Paris apartment, she feels increasingly suffocated by fleeting relationships, rising anxiety, and the grip of an alcohol addiction that is quietly tightening around her life. Amid the chaos, however, her devotion to her sick younger sister and a tender, blossoming romance with Pauline offer Garance a fragile lifeline. As these bonds deepen, she finds the strength to confront the darkness she has long avoided – setting her on a difficult but transformative journey to self-renewal.

title: Brother Verses Brother
description:
US · 92 min · Special Screenings
Codependent twin musicians Ari and Ethan Gold have one night to find three things: love, a song, and their father - a 99-year-old Beat Generation poet, the last of his kind. Their search plays out in 90 minutes of “Live Cinema,” according to the precepts of Executive Producer Francis Ford Coppola, delivering a single unbroken journey through San Francisco's North Beach, toward one final performance, captured just weeks before their father’s death.

title: Balkanika - Dark Side
description:
Bosnia and Herzegovina · 148 min · BH Film - Feature Films, Submissions
In Livno, a young smuggler nicknamed Struja and his crew transport drugs from Bosnia and Herzegovina into Croatia for a powerful crime boss known as Oluja. Their operation becomes complicated when Bakar’s girlfriend Layla, a Syrian migrant, remains in town with a bag of explosives she was supposed to carry further into Europe. When Bakar refuses to return the explosives, dangerous men arrive in Livno searching for Layla and the bag. What began as a local criminal enterprise turns into a fight for survival, where love, friendship, and loyalty collide with a threat far greater than any of them had imagined.

title: Queen at Sea
description:
UK, US · 121 min · Gala Screening
Amanda and her stepfather Martin struggle with a moral issue that divides them. Has Amanda’s mother, who is experiencing advanced dementia, lost the ability to make critical decisions in her own best interest? If so, who is responsible – a spouse, a child, an institution – for making such a determination? As Amanda and Martin are forced to make increasingly difficult choices, the repercussions spiral out of their control.

title: Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma
description:
US, Canada · 112 min · Kinoscope Surreal
The infamous Camp Miasma slasher-film franchise is getting rebooted yet again. But when the latest instalment’s director becomes obsessed with the mysterious, reclusive actor who played the “final girl” in the original film, a whole new kind of slasher emerges from the bottom of the lake.

title: No Fairy Dust
description:
Serbia, Italy, Netherlands, Croatia, Slovenia, Montenegro · 100 min · Midnight Screenings
Marija, an ice skater, lives on the outskirts of Belgrade with her truck-driving father. Crushed by grief over the premature death of her mother, Maria does not know how to express her sexuality. She perceives this failure as her big, haunting secret. When Marija’s father becomes close with a woman, he invites her and her two daughters to move in. Marija supports her father’s choice, but understands she cannot trust her new stepmother. The family struggles financially, so Marija is expected to earn extra money. She wants to protect her father by hiding from him the work assignments that take her into the world where women are sexually exploited. This only increases the pressure on her already suppressed sexuality.

title: Bruca Braca Bruda Brada - Zombie Apocalypse
description:
Bosnia and Herzegovina · 70 min · BH Film - Feature Films, Midnight Screenings
The year is 2045: humankind has almost defeated death, but in some parts of the world the problem of the parking-space shortage has yet to be resolved. The most powerful political leader of a Sarajevo municipality decides to implement a controversial idea and build a parking lot atop an old local cemetery. Of course, it is just the drop that causes the glass to overflow.

title: Supporting Role
description:
Georgia, Estonia, Turkey · 139 min · Competition Programme – Narrative Feature Film
A retired Georgian film star, once accustomed to playing heroic leading roles, embarks on a cathartic journey after a casting session with a young female director, who offers him the supporting role of a bizarre and deeply unsympathetic character in her debut feature. He leaves the audition unconvinced, even slightly offended. Yet as the story unfolds, he gradually surrenders to the role, becoming captivated by the strange and the unknown. The experience awakens something within him, setting in motion an irreversible process of self-transformation.

title: MASTERCLASS: Emily Watson
description:
90 min
Moderated Interview in the form of a conversation with Jury president and Recipient of the Honorary Heart of Sarajevo Award, Emily Watson, where she will share his knowledge and experiences with both the Festival audience and participants.

title: All We Have Is Us
description:
Chile · 79 min · Human Rights Day
ALL WE HAVE IS US connects two distant yet deeply intertwined territories: the Atacama Desert in Chile and the Jadar Valley in Serbia, both threatened by lithium mining projects led by Rio Tinto, the world’s second-largest mining company. Over five years, the film closely chronicles Leyla, an Aymara journalist and land defender, and Bojana, a Serbian actor fighting to protect her mother’s village. Through protests, high-stakes public events, and intimate everyday moments, we witness the raw personal stakes of environmental struggle. As their paths cross, these women weave a transcontinental network of solidarity with local farmers, activists, and artists. These organic relationships become their deepest source of strength, sustaining them through systemic pressure, displacement risks, exhaustion, and uncertainty. Blending character-driven storytelling with public media discourse, ALL WE HAVE IS US  strips away the polished corporate facade of the green economy. At its heart, the film is a powerful examination of belonging, resistance, and the urgent question of what “progress” really means, who gets to decide, and at what cost.

title: Heysel 85
description:
Belgium, Netherlands, Germany · 91 min · Kinoscope
When violence erupts before the 1985 European Cup Final between Liverpool and Juventus at Brussels’ Heysel Stadium, killing thirty-nine people, the mayor’s daughter and a journalist with Italian roots are drawn into the heart of the tragedy, caught between professional duty, family loyalty, and moral responsibility.

title: Sink
description:
Jordan, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, France, Estonia · 88 min · Sarajevo Film Festival Partner Presents
When her teenage son Basil is suspended from school after a troubling outburst during his senior year, Nadia is determined to help him, convincing herself he just needs guidance. As Basil’s mental state slowly unravels, however, Nadia ignores the warning signs, sinking deeper into denial as disaster approaches.

title: Soil and Wings
description:
Serbia, North Macedonia · 77 min · The Béla Tarr in Sarajevo Tribute
In the North Macedonian village of Kanatlar, Ayten and Erdoğan raise their children, balancing the eight-hundred-year-old Bektashi Sufi teachings with the struggles of modern life. In this tobacco-growing valley, a Turkish Muslim community devoted to faith, family, and tradition allows gender equality to flourish quietly, rooted in the belief that all beings are equal.

title: Mother
description:
Belgium, North Macedonia, Denmark, Sweden, Bosnia and Herzegovina · 104 min · BH Film - Feature Films, In Focus
Kolkata, India, August 1948. Teresa, Mother Superior of the convent of the Sisters of Loreto, is anxiously waiting for the letter that will finally allow her to leave her monastery and create a new order in response to the call she has received from God. And just as everything seems ready, she finds herself faced with a dilemma that challenges her own ambitions and faith at a major turning point in her life.

title: Splish Splash Forever!
description:
Switzerland · 88 min · Children's Programme, Submissions
Pola (11) wants to save the swimming pool “Splish Splash” from being closed so that her best friend will come back. Her friend’s parents, who ran the café, emigrated when the pool was shut down. But her friend does not return, and Pola learns to let go of the past and stand up for a greater cause. In the end, she has not only won the fight for the pool, but also gained new friendships.

title: The Dreamed Adventure
description:
Germany, France, Bulgaria, Austria · 167 min · Kinoscope
In Svilengrad, a small town on the Bulgarian border, Veska crosses paths with Said, an old acquaintance whose car has been stolen. Offering her help, Veska brings him along to the excavation site where she is working as an archaeologist. As they reconnect, she is pulled more into the shady world Said has emerged from, and she soon embarks on an exploration of the criminal ties lurking beneath the surface of this seemingly innocent town on the outskirts of Europe. As figures from her past start to close in, Veska is forced to confront the truth about the town and her experiences.

title: A Hero
description:
Iran, France · 127 min · Tribute To
Rahim is in prison because of a debt he was unable to repay. During a two-day leave, he tries to convince his creditor to withdraw his complaint against the payment of part of the sum. But things don't go as planned...

title: Antigone, The Docutragedy
description:
US · 75 min · Special Screenings
ANTIGONE, THE DOCUTRAGEDY uses the restored recording of a small independent 1995 Los Angeles production of "Antigone," starring Mira Furlan, as the foundation for an original cinematic journey. As three decades separate the performance from the present, the production reveals itself to be even more relevant and prophetic than when it was first staged. Transcending its theatrical origins, the film becomes a documentary about our world — about the United States, Hollywood, war, exile, art, and the extraordinary people whose lives echo Sophocles's timeless tragedy.

title: The Balkan Cowboy
description:
Ireland, Croatia · 93 min · Competition Programme - Documentary Film, Submissions
Artist Dragana Jurišić travels to the town of Bijeljina, Bosnia and Herzegovina, to stage a short film in the style of the mythical cult Western director Hari Džekson (Harry Jackson). In an attempt to uncover the story of Džekson’s life and legacy, Jurišić embarks on making a Western with the local community. She meets his former collaborators, family members, and local residents, piecing together memories of Džekson’s town before the war and getting to know its inhabitants today.  The resulting documentary becomes an exploration of the impact of war on Džekson, Jurišić herself, and the town. It also asks whether the spirit of Hari Džekson still exists today.

title: Not a Hero
description:
India, Singapore · 98 min · Children's Programme
Mivan, 11, a city raised boy, is sent to his ancestral village to stay withhis young aunt, Pahi. Used to the speed and comforts of urban life, he finds the village slow, unfamiliar, and difficult to accept. His relationship with Pahi is distant, shaped by unspoken tensions and unresolved feelings from the past. As Mivan is drawn into village routines, school, and new friendships, he begins to experience a world where time moves differently and nothing comes easily.

title: Bruca Braca Bruda Brada - Zombie Apocalypse
description:
Bosnia and Herzegovina · 70 min · BH Film - Feature Films, Midnight Screenings
The year is 2045: humankind has almost defeated death, but in some parts of the world the problem of the parking-space shortage has yet to be resolved. The most powerful political leader of a Sarajevo municipality decides to implement a controversial idea and build a parking lot atop an old local cemetery. Of course, it is just the drop that causes the glass to overflow.

title: Filipiñana
description:
Singapore, UK, Philippines, France, Netherlands · 110 min · Kinoscope
New tee-girl Isabel feels strangely drawn to Dr Palanca, the president of the country club where she works. As she starts to piece together a picture of the violence that lies beneath the country club’s pristine surface, however, Isable comes to realise that what began as an innocent infatuation with Dr Palanca is actually rooted in a more sinister shared history.

title: Supporting Role
description:
Georgia, Estonia, Turkey · 139 min · Competition Programme – Narrative Feature Film
A retired Georgian film star, once accustomed to playing heroic leading roles, embarks on a cathartic journey after a casting session with a young female director, who offers him the supporting role of a bizarre and deeply unsympathetic character in her debut feature. He leaves the audition unconvinced, even slightly offended. Yet as the story unfolds, he gradually surrenders to the role, becoming captivated by the strange and the unknown. The experience awakens something within him, setting in motion an irreversible process of self-transformation.

title: Black Money for White Nights
description:
Bulgaria, Greece · 94 min · Adriatic Audience Award
Marina, a maternity nurse, and her husband Gosha, a railway dispatcher, have spent years collecting small bribes to be able to afford their dream trip to St. Petersburg to witness the White Nights. When Russia invades Ukraine and the travel agency vanishes with their savings, their dream — and the illusion of control — collapses. Gosha ends up in the hospital, beaten while trying to recover the money and long-buried betrayals surface, forcing the couple to confront the lies their life was built on and to search among the ruins for a trace of dignity and grace.

title: Manhunt
description:
Canada · 103 min · Kinoscope
Two young men flee their dead-end lives on a road trip into the northern frontier. Recasting true crime as parable, MANHUNt explores loneliness, masculinity, and the colonial urge to begin anew – until the search for meaning erupts into violence.

title: Sheep in the Box
description:
Japan · 126 min · Summer Screen
Grieving Kakeru, their young son, who died in mysterious circumstances, Otone and her husband Kensuke turn to REbirth, a company that assists the bereaved by allowing them to spend more time with their deceased loved ones. Using AI-generated robotics, the company supplies the parents with a state-of-the-art humanoid replication of Kakeru. Initially, the humanoid is barely communicative; it develops rapidly, however, and appears to have memories that are logically impossible for it to have access to. Otone and Kensuke are perplexed to find themselves drawing closer and closer to what appears more and more to be their son.

title: Palestine 36
description:
Palestine, UK, France, Denmark, Norway, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Jordan, United Arab Emirates · 119 min · Open Air
In 1936, as the British Empire tightens its grip on Palestine, Yusuf is caught between his village home and his work in Jerusalem. Amidst an anti-colonial revolt, and Jewish refugees fleeing persecution from Europe, all sides converge in a decisive moment for the entire region.

title: The Virus of Pathological Kindness
venue: UNIQA Open Air Cinema Stari Grad
description:
Serbia, Croatia, Slovenia, Bosnia and Herzegovina · 99 min · Open Air Premiere
On a snowy Zagreb night in 1983, a stranger inexplicably turns up at Zorka Vasiljević’s flat claiming he has arrived from the future using a time machine. His stunning predictions of the events of that night and disturbing stories of what lies ahead force Zorka to decide if she believes him or not. Is the future of humankind really dependent on her decisions?

title: Guggi
description:
Ireland · 77 min · Special Screenings
From the streets of Dublin to the walls of major galleries, GUGGI follows the life and work of Irish artist Guggi, exploring the friendships, struggles, and inner forces that shaped one of Ireland's most distinctive creative voices.

title: Hidden People
description:
Slovenia, Serbia, Iceland · 97 min · Open Air Premiere
Guti (35) and Sig (50) wake up beaten, hungover, and handcuffed together on a riverbank near Ljubljana. Sig, obviously a tourist, suffers from memory loss and can’t remember where he is from and why he is - as he thinks - stuck in Slovakia. Together with Guti, they embark on a journey to recover Sig’s passport and identity and, in the meantime, work on Guti’s dream project: a river raft that will hopefully rebuild Guti’s life that has fallen victim to bad divorce, failed bank loans, vicious bureaucracy, and many, many bad neighbors.

title: The Birthday Party
description:
France · 114 min · Summer Screen
Thomas, Nora, and their teenage daughter Ida live on remote marshland. Social contact is limited, as they only have one neighbour, Cristina, an Italian painter. As the two households plan a surprise birthday party for Nora, strange disturbances begin to occur and unease rolls over the marsh.

title: Congo Boy
description:
Central African Republic, France, Congo - Kinshasa, Italy · 95 min · Kinoscope, TeenArena
Bangui, Central African Republic. Seventeen-year-old Robert dreams of a career in music, but civil war is tearing the country apart. When both his parents are thrown into prison, he is left to look after his four younger siblings on his own, juggling daily life, odd jobs, school exams, and concert stages, determined to follow his dream.

title: Our Father
description:
Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina · 89 min · BH Film - Feature Films, Submissions
When Dejan arrives at a monastery-based rehabilitation community for people struggling with addiction, he is welcomed by the charismatic Father Branko, who assigns him a mentor, Mionica, a former addict. Within a community governed by strict rules, harsh punishments, and brutal methods of treatment, Dejan quickly becomes Father Branko's favorite. But when footage exposing violence inside the community is leaked to the public, Dejan-now Branko's right-hand man-finds himself torn between loyalty to the man and the system that gave his life new purpose, and the demands of his own conscience.

title: The Vault
description:
Slovenia, Croatia, Montenegro · 100 min · Avant Premiere Series
Creator: Matevž LuzarWhen night guard Sonja Kern wakes up on the floor of a robbed bank vault, she cannot remember a thing. There is no sign of forced entry, no alarm, and nothing on the security cameras. The only person found inside, she is also the easiest to blame: a broke single mother with a police record. Inspector Deja Kolenc builds the case on instinct, while Maksimilijan Sotler, a coldly precise insurance investigator, approaches the same crime from the opposite side. Slowly, the structure behind the robbery begins to surface, leading to a mayoral campaign, a silent financier, and a document that powerful men will kill for. As Sonja's memory gradually returns, one beat at a time, she is forced to choose between the truth and the only person she cares about.

title: A Separation
description:
Iran · 123 min · Gala Screening - Tribute To, Tribute To
When his wife leaves him, Nader hires a young woman to take care of his suffering father. But he doesn’t know his new maid is not only pregnant, but also working without the permission of her unstable husband. Soon, Nader finds himself entangled in a web of lies, manipulation and public confrontation.

title: Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma
description:
US, Canada · 112 min · Kinoscope Surreal
The infamous Camp Miasma slasher-film franchise is getting rebooted yet again. But when the latest instalment’s director becomes obsessed with the mysterious, reclusive actor who played the “final girl” in the original film, a whole new kind of slasher emerges from the bottom of the lake.

title: Saccharine
description:
Australia · 120 min · Kinoscope Surreal
Hana, a lovelorn medical student struggling with body image and disordered eating, becomes obsessed with a mysterious weight-loss craze after discovering a pill made from human ashes. As the miraculous treatment transforms her body, she is haunted by the vengeful spirit of the woman whose remains she has consumed.

title: Skateboarding Is Not for Girls
description:
North Macedonia, Belgium, Slovenia, Croatia · 82 min · Competition Programme – Narrative Feature Film, TeenArena
Eleven-year-old Adela and her elder sister Zara share a deep bond shaped by their navigation of two contradictory worlds. At school, they are typical, rebellious teens with skateboards, social media, crop tops, and boyfriends. After school, in a quiet and disciplined mode, they help their mother with cleaning jobs to make ends meet. When poverty shakes the family, Adela tries to find a way to save her sister – still a minor – from a fate that is becoming almost inevitable: an arranged marriage.

title: MASTERCLASS: Asghar Farhadi
description:
90 min
Moderated Interview in the form of a conversation with Honorary Heart of Sarajevo Award Recipient Asghar Farhadi, where he will share his knowledge and experiences with both the Festival audience and participants.

title: Silent Friend
description:
Germany, China, France, Hungary · 145 min · Kinoscope
In the heart of a botanical garden in a medieval university town in Germany stands a majestic ginkgo tree. Over the course of a century, this silent witness has observed the quiet rhythms of transformation across three human lives. In 2020, a neuroscientist from Hong Kong who explores the infant mind begins an unexpected experiment with the old tree. In 1972, a young student is profoundly changed by the simple act of observing and connecting with a geranium. In 1908, the university’s first female student discovers, through the lens of photography, sacred patterns of the universe hidden within the humblest of plants. We follow their clumsy, awkward attempts to connect — each of them deeply rooted in their own present — as they are transformed by the quiet, enduring, and mysterious power of nature.

title: You Don't Belong Here
description:
Romania · 154 min · Competition Programme – Narrative Feature Film
Marius, the chief medical officer at a hospital in his small hometown, is raising his teenage son Ioan alone after the death of his wife. Marius is a confident professional who has no idea what his son gets up to at night: cycling through town vandalising cars with a gang of masked vigilantes. Marius’s world is shaken when he learns the police have come to suspect his son of murder.

description:
Iceland, Sweden, Poland · 106 min · The Béla Tarr in Sarajevo Tribute
A childless couple in rural Iceland make an alarming discovery one day in their sheep barn. They soon face the consequences of defying the will of nature in this dark and atmospheric folktale.
