title: Elvis, My Neighbor
description:
Bosnia and Herzegovina · 88 min · BH Film - Documentary Feature Film, Submissions
Duško Mandić was one of those people who, at first glance, looked like he was stuck in time. I moved into a new building, and I wanted to - I didn't want to, I soon got to know him - a weirdo in a red Elvis department, with a rockabilly haircut, sunglasses, and a royal ring, which was almost his trademark. There wasn't a day that we didn't meet. There wasn't a day when one of the neighbors didn't make fun of him, some considered him eccentric, and some simply turned their heads when they saw him walking down the street or driving his unique electric moped. At the time I thought he was just another one of those people who wanted to get attention, but that was just my superficial assessment. Everything changed one afternoon when I happened to hear him sing.

title: 3 Days in September
description:
Romania · 78 min · In Focus
On Bianca's wedding day, in the midst of the final preparations, her fiancé’s mistress crashes the nuptials. Bianca is shocked and flees on a tourist train, launching a real-time odyssey of chaotic escape and surreal encounters through the seaside resort in the off season. Rejecting her old life, she transforms her humiliation into a liberating night of rebellion.

title: Heysel 85
description:
Belgium, Netherlands, Germany · 91 min · Kinoscope
When violence erupts before the 1985 European Cup Final between Liverpool and Juventus at Brussels’ Heysel Stadium, killing thirty-nine people, the mayor’s daughter and a journalist with Italian roots are drawn into the heart of the tragedy, caught between professional duty, family loyalty, and moral responsibility.

title: Parallel Tales
description:
France, Belgium, Italy · 140 min · Tribute To
In search of inspiration for her new novel, Sylvie spies on her neighbors across the street. When she hires young Adam to help her with her daily routine, she has no idea that he will turn her life and her work upside down, until the fiction she had imagined surpasses the reality of them all. PARALLEL TALES is freely based on the film DEKALOG 6 written by Krzysztof Piesiewicz and Krzysztof Kieślowski.

title: Coward
description:
Belgium, France, Netherlands · 120 min · Kinoscope
As the First World War drags on, Pierre, a soldier newly arrived at the front, is eager to prove himself. Behind the lines, he meets Francis, who decides to lift the spirits of his comrades by putting together a theatre show. While the violence continues, both men try to find ways to escape the brutality of war, even if only for a moment.

description:
Greece, France, Denmark · 87 min · Competition Programme - Documentary Film
George, a shy teenager with misaligned eyes, struggles to connect with others after his parents’ traumatic divorce. Finding refuge in the world of insects, he bonds with a cricket named Isabella, who inspires him to reimagine his place in the world. Through a portrait of transformation and self-discovery, BUGBOY reminds us that even the smallest creatures can help us find where we belong.

title: Chronicles From the Siege
description:
Algeria, France, Palestine · 98 min · Dealing with the past
When their city is placed under siege, the lives of a group of ordinary people are turned upside down, forcing each of them to confront impossible choices in pursuit of survival in a war zone. Bodies and minds are equally under attack; ordinary people are forced to reckon with starvation, inadequate medical treatment, snipers, and bomb blasts as they continue to live their lives, seeking friendship, love, intimacy, and the pleasure of smoking a cigarette. At one point, a small group of cinephiles who are sheltering in their neighbourhood video store are confronted with the moral conundrum of whether or not to burn the movies they have rented – and that they cherish – to keep warm. The psychological impact of the siege is boldly expressed in writing on the door of one of the characters's homes: “I don’t see my life outside the confines of the siege. And I don’t see an end to the siege outside of the confines of my life.”

title: Truly Naked
description:
Netherlands, Belgium, France · 102 min · Adriatic Audience Award
Alec, a soft-spoken, introverted teenager, has always viewed life through the lens of his father’s small-time pornography business. When they relocate from London to a sleepy seaside town, Alec hopes for a fresh start, trying to make friends without revealing his unconventional life. Everything shifts when he meets the fiercely independent Nina, whose convictions redefine the world he has grown up in. As their relationship deepens, Alec’s understanding of sexuality and desire begins to shift.

description:
France, Latvia, Germany · 140 min · Open Air
Russia, 2022. When Gleb, a successful company director, finds himself under siege from mounting corporate pressures and an increasingly unstable world, the collapse of his carefully ordered life accelerates towards violence.

title: 3 Weeks After
venue: UNIQA Open Air Cinema Stari Grad
description:
Serbia, Bulgaria, Italy, Croatia, Luxembourg · 95 min · Open Air Premiere
It all begins as a typical school trip. A bus, school friends, professors, casual jokes, small excitements, and the well-known temporary sense of freedom children get when travelling. Gradually, however, it becomes clear that all is not well in the small community. Daily glances, teasing, and silences hide something nobody wants to talk about. Zoza is burdened by the death of his best friend, who committed suicide three weeks before the school trip. When he decides to talk about his school friends’ failure to speak up about the brutal mistreatment of his friend and their decision to turn their gaze away from it, all attention turns to him. From that moment, he becomes the next victim. He escapes into the woods and then into a cave, where the only person he can still trust finds him. She betrays him, too. After what happens to him, something in Zoza shifts for good. He returns at dawn. Changed.

title: Stand Together As One: The Famine, The Music, The Impact
description:
US, Kenya · 59 min · Special Screenings
Forty years after the recording of "We Are the World," the pop anthem still resonates for music lovers worldwide... and the global concert Live Aid remains the benchmark for what’s possible when musicians come together in a common cause. When drought hit Ethiopia in 1983, millions of people in the war-ravaged nation were denied food relief by a ruthless dictatorship. More than one million people starved to death. The treacherous war zone didn’t stop Kenyan photojournalist Mohamed Amin or his BBC colleagues Michael Buerk and Mike Wooldridge. The skilled frontline team risked their lives to tell the truth behind what many consider the worst humanitarian disaster of the twentieth century. Inspired by their historic global report, musicians chose to stand together as one.

title: All of a Sudden
description:
France, Japan, Germany, Belgium · 196 min · Summer Screen
As the director of a care facility for the elderly, Marie-Lou strives to introduce an innovative care philosophy based on listening and respecting residents’ dignity, despite resistance from some members of her staff. Her encounter with Mari, a Japanese theatre director battling cancer, will profoundly reshape Marie-Lou's path. By forming a deep, supportive friendship, the two women join forces in a shared struggle to “make the impossible possible."

title: Gentle Monster
venue: BH Telecom Open Air Cinema Centar
description:
Austria, Germany, France · 114 min · Summer Screen
Lucy, a concert pianist, has just relocated her family from the city to a country house in the hope of easing her husband Philip’s severe burnout. Before they have a chance to set up their new home, an early-morning police visit tears their world apart. Isolated and desperate to protect her young son, Lucy must face the situation alone, trapped between the man she loves and the fear of what he may have done.

title: Deepest dive
description:
Bosnia and Herzegovina · 53 min · BH Film - Documentary Feature Film, Submissions
What happens when a city that has kept the tradition of diving from the Old Bridge for nearly five centuries decides to share it with the world? What was once a rite of passage — of growing up, belonging, and earning respect among Mostar's people — today shares the stage with the world's best divers at the Red Bull Cliff Diving World Series. Through poetic narration, authentic testimonies from traditional divers, archival footage, and symbolic visual reconstructions, the film explores the meeting of local heritage and modern cliff diving, revealing how a city with such a strong sense of identity embraces the new while staying true to itself. At the heart of the film are not just the dives, but the people who, through them, have preserved their city's identity for centuries.

description:
Romania, France, Norway, Sweden, Denmark · 146 min · Summer Screen
The Gheorghius, a devout Romanian Norwegian couple, resettle in a village set in a distant fjord, where they become close to their neighbours, the Halbergs. Their children bond despite their different education. When adolescent Elia shows up at school with some bruises on her body, the community asks itself if the traditional education the Gheorghiu children get from their parents could have anything to do with it.Porodica Gheorghiu, rumunsko-norveški par vjernika s djecom, seli se u udaljeni fjord gdje se zbližavaju sa svojim susjedima, porodicom Halberg. Djeca dviju porodica se sprijateljuju uprkos razlikama u obrazovanju. Kada se adolescentica Elia Gheorghiu pojavi u školi s masnicama na tijelu, zajednica počne propitivati da li tradicionalno obrazovanje koje djeca dobijaju od svojih roditelja ima neke veze s tim.

title: Bugboy
description:
Greece, France, Denmark · 87 min · Competition Programme - Documentary Film
George, a shy teenager with misaligned eyes, struggles to connect with others after his parents’ traumatic divorce. Finding refuge in the world of insects, he bonds with a cricket named Isabella, who inspires him to reimagine his place in the world. Through a portrait of transformation and self-discovery, BUGBOY reminds us that even the smallest creatures can help us find where we belong.

Aziz, a professor at Ankara University, receives a "yellow letter" arbitrarily informing him of his dismissal. When his wife Derya, a famous actress at the national theater, receives one too, it is the final blow for the couple. Both condemned for their ideas, they are forced to seek refuge in Istanbul with Aziz's mother. The compromise between this new precariousness and their political commitment will put their marriage to the test.

title: Silent Friend
description:
Germany, China, France, Hungary · 145 min · Kinoscope
In the heart of a botanical garden in a medieval university town in Germany stands a majestic ginkgo tree. Over the course of a century, this silent witness has observed the quiet rhythms of transformation across three human lives. In 2020, a neuroscientist from Hong Kong who explores the infant mind begins an unexpected experiment with the old tree. In 1972, a young student is profoundly changed by the simple act of observing and connecting with a geranium. In 1908, the university’s first female student discovers, through the lens of photography, sacred patterns of the universe hidden within the humblest of plants. We follow their clumsy, awkward attempts to connect — each of them deeply rooted in their own present — as they are transformed by the quiet, enduring, and mysterious power of nature.

Marius’s world is shaken when he learns the police have come to suspect his son of murder.

title: We Shall Live Together
description:
Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina · 75 min · BH Film - Documentary Feature Film, Competition Programme - Documentary Film, Submissions
At the outbreak of war in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Roko Markovina – a socialist who served as a member of the country’s parliament between 1990 and 1996 – decided to stay in Mostar, his hometown, with his family, convinced it was his moral duty despite the ethnic conflict ravaging the town. Roko’s anti-nationalist convictions inspired him to vote against the Dayton Peace Agreement – an act that made him a symbol of Bosnia and Herzegovina’s leftists, but also a target of the nationalists’ scorn. He paid a high price to preserve his moral integrity, losing his nation, political party, city, and home. Three decades later, Markovina and his wife live in voluntary exile on a Mediterranean island, but his decisions still strain his relationship with his sons. Through their meetings, WE SHALL LIVE TOGETHER explores the legacy of war and family division, as well as what is required to be able to move on with life.

description:

As the First World War drags on, Pierre, a soldier newly arrived at the front, is eager to prove himself. Behind the lines, he meets Francis, who decides to lift the spirits of his comrades by putting together a theatre show. While the violence continues, both men try to find ways to escape the brutality of war, even if only for a moment.

title: Identity
description:
Croatia · 74 min · Dealing with the past, Submissions
Ajna, Alen, and Lejla were born after their mothers were raped in the war. Ajna was kept by her mother, while Alen and Lejla were adopted. They grew up and lived differently and learned the truth about their origins in various ways, but they are bound by an inner feeling that is incomprehensible to all other people. Their stories intertwine through the fight for the legal status of war victims, very personal searches and public appearances, while the film explores identity and trauma, as well as the possibilities of community and belonging, through archives and an observational approach.

title: The Virus of Pathological Kindness
description:
Serbia, Croatia, Slovenia, Bosnia and Herzegovina · 99 min · Open Air Premiere
On a snowy Zagreb night in 1983, a stranger inexplicably turns up at Zorka Vasiljević’s flat claiming he has arrived from the future using a time machine. His stunning predictions of the events of that night and disturbing stories of what lies ahead force Zorka to decide if she believes him or not. Is the future of humankind really dependent on her decisions?

title: Home
description:
Denmark · 104 min · Open Air Premiere, Submissions
In 1991, amid the Balkan region's dissolution and prompted by the unfolding events, six-year-old Maja and her parents decide to journey from Yugoslavia to Denmark. Their encounter with the promised land proves to be a challenging ordeal for the small family, however, and particularly for Maja. She observes in wonder as her parents desperately try to adapt to an entirely new world. Witnessing her parents' difficulties, Maja quickly learns to speak Danish and consequently shoulders the responsibility of an adult to support them. Years later, despite achieving success, Maja grapples with conflicting emotions, recognising the sacrifices her parents made that shaped her life – for, as we know well, everything comes with its price.

title: Parallel Tales
description:
France, Belgium, Italy · 140 min · Tribute To
In search of inspiration for her new novel, Sylvie spies on her neighbors across the street. When she hires young Adam to help her with her daily routine, she has no idea that he will turn her life and her work upside down, until the fiction she had imagined surpasses the reality of them all. PARALLEL TALES is freely based on the film DEKALOG 6 written by Krzysztof Piesiewicz and Krzysztof Kieślowski.

title: No Man's Land
description:
France, Belgium, Italy, UK, Slovenia, Bosnia and Herzegovina · 98 min · Open Air
A quarter of a century after its original premiere, NO MAN'S LAND, directed by Danis Tanović, returns to the Sarajevo Film Festival. This festival screening will mark the world premiere of the digitally restored version of the film, which has left an indelible mark on both regional and global cinema. Festival audiences will have the exclusive opportunity to be the first to experience the newly restored 4K version, completed by Studiocanal using the original 35mm camera negative. NO MAN'S LAND had its world premiere on 12 May 2001 at the Cannes Film Festival, where it received the award for Best Screenplay. By August of the same year, it was presented to domestic audiences at the Sarajevo Film Festival, winning both the Best Film Award and the Audience Award. This marked the beginning of an exceptional international journey, culminating on 24 March 2002 with the Academy Award® for Best Foreign Language Film. Emerging from the lived experience and realities of the region, the film’s universal story of war, absurdity, and humanity resonated with critics and audiences worldwide, earning Bosnia and Herzegovina one of its most significant international cultural distinctions.

description:
Bosnia and Herzegovina · 102 min · BH Film - Feature Films, Open Air Premiere
Mirsad is a sixty-two-year-old electrician who was raised and lives in a patriarchal society. His daily routine changes after the sudden death of his wife, Enisa. Mirsad is left alone while his grown children live their own lives. As he tries to get used to a life without his wife, he realises that he took her for granted and had never given her the love and care she deserved. Mirsad’s relationship with his estranged son worsens after he discovers the son lives with a male friend. While his best friend tries to convince him to find a new wife, Mirsad starts questioning his life and his relationships with people, but it is too late for him to change the way he treated Enisa. Soon, Mirsad realises his daughter lives a life similar to that of her mother.

title: Fjord
description:
Romania, France, Norway, Sweden, Denmark · 146 min · Summer Screen
The Gheorghius, a devout Romanian Norwegian couple, resettle in a village set in a distant fjord, where they become close to their neighbours, the Halbergs. Their children bond despite their different education. When adolescent Elia shows up at school with some bruises on her body, the community asks itself if the traditional education the Gheorghiu children get from their parents could have anything to do with it.Porodica Gheorghiu, rumunsko-norveški par vjernika s djecom, seli se u udaljeni fjord gdje se zbližavaju sa svojim susjedima, porodicom Halberg. Djeca dviju porodica se sprijateljuju uprkos razlikama u obrazovanju. Kada se adolescentica Elia Gheorghiu pojavi u školi s masnicama na tijelu, zajednica počne propitivati da li tradicionalno obrazovanje koje djeca dobijaju od svojih roditelja ima neke veze s tim.
